title: TestPrep Question
description: Standard question format for all certifications in the test-prep skill

domain.description: Domain number as defined in blueprint.md

difficulty.description: Difficulty mapped to cert level nomenclature

question.description: Full question text. Should end with a question mark.

options.description: Exactly 4 answer options. Order matters — 'correct' indexes into this array.

correct.description: 0-based index of the correct option in the options array

explanation.description: Why the correct answer is right AND why each wrong option is wrong. Educational, not just confirmatory.

trick.description: Human-readable description of the distractor trap used in this question. Empty string if none.

trick_pattern.description: Which distractor pattern this question exercises

source.description: Where this question content came from e.g. 'Official study guide Obj 2.3'

timeLimitSeconds.description: Suggested per-question timer. Defaults: foundational=30, associate=60, professional=90

examples.question: What is the PRIMARY architectural advantage of GPUs over CPUs for deep learning training?
options: GPUs have faster individual processing cores than CPU cores
GPUs contain thousands of smaller cores optimized for massively parallel computation
GPUs have larger cache sizes than CPUs
GPUs use a simpler instruction set for matrix operations
examples.explanation: GPUs are NOT faster per individual core — CPU cores run at higher clock speeds. The GPU advantage is massive parallelism: thousands of simpler cores executing simultaneously, perfectly suited to the matrix math of deep learning. Option C is wrong: CPUs actually have larger per-core cache. Option D is wrong: both use complex instruction sets; the advantage is architectural, not ISA-based.
examples.trick: Trap: 'faster cores' sounds plausible but reverses the truth. CPU cores are individually faster. GPU advantage = parallel quantity, not per-core speed.
